payload.title: Honeymoon Planning Service and How It Works
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, planning a destination wedding or already engaged, who want a luxury honeymoon but have no time to piece it together themselves, and want a plain account of what a honeymoon planning service actually does, how it works with Wedded Wonderland, what to decide before they enquire and what to ask any planner before agreeing to anything.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation at /wonderland-concierge so one advisor can plan the honeymoon, on its own or alongside the wedding.
payload.angle: Page-one results for 'honeymoon planning service' are mostly agency and registry sales pages that promise perks, upgrades, 'free' extras and hand-picked resorts, rarely say how the process works or what it costs to engage, and are often US-centric. This guide makes no perk claims. It explains the service plainly, shows exactly how it works with Wedded Wonderland using only the brand-facts steps 1 and 2 and standing claims (one Wedded Advisor start to finish, fee agreed in writing before any work begins, inclusions confirmed in writing before you commit, your time zone, quotes in AUD, travel planned anywhere in the world), and is the only result that treats the honeymoon as part of a destination wedding: one advisor across both, AUD quotes, timing, and the name on passports and tickets after marriage only as Smartraveller states it. It then gives the reader what sales pages never do: a short list of what to decide before enquiring and a neutral checklist of questions to ask any honeymoon planner (fee and inclusions in writing, both sets of terms, insurance timing, the exchange rate on AUD quotes, supplier commissions).
must_include: Intro with a direct answer in the first 100 words: a honeymoon planning service is one person who plans and books the honeymoon for you, with the fee and inclusions confirmed in writing; framed as easier, never exclusive. Then exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways (what the service does; with Wedded Wonderland one Wedded Advisor plans it start to finish, fee agreed in writing first; planning it alongside the wedding keeps one contact, AUD quotes and timing together; decide dates, length, style and must-haves, and ask any planner about fee, inclusions, terms, insurance, exchange rate and commissions).

What a honeymoon planning service does: general, neutral description of planning and booking on the couple's behalf; no perks, no named resorts, airlines or hotels, no 'best'. Link /travel-guides/travel-advisor-benefits (draft sister article; check live before publish) for the broader case for an advisor.

How it works with Wedded Wonderland: brand-facts steps 1 ('Tell us anything.') and 2 ('Meet your Wedded Advisor, and agree the fee.' with 'The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.') only, plus standing claims in brand-facts wording: 'One Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact.'; 'The advisor confirms inclusions in writing before the couple commits.'; 'Advisor works in the couple's time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.'; travel planned anywhere in the world (from 'Plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.'). State that honeymoon-only planning follows the same Wedded Advisor process (confirmed 2026-11-16). Link /wonderland-concierge (anchor 'Wedded Concierge', UTM primary).

Planning the honeymoon alongside the wedding: one advisor across both, quotes in AUD, timing (straight after or later; link /expert-advice/a-guide-on-when-to-go-on-honeymoon), and the name on passports and tickets after marriage stated only as Smartraveller states it [[VERIFY: Smartraveller guidance on travelling soon after marriage, passport name matching tickets, as at November 2026]]. Link up to /destination-honeymoon-packages and /travel without competing for package terms.

What to decide before you enquire, as prompts not rules: dates, length (link /expert-advice/how-long-is-a-honeymoon-a-guide-by-destination), style (slow, adventurous, one place or several), must-haves. No prices or budget figures.

Questions to ask any honeymoon planner, as a numbered neutral checklist: Is the fee agreed in writing before work begins? Which inclusions will you confirm in writing? What are both sets of terms (yours and each supplier's) for changes and cancellations? When should we take out travel insurance (pointing to Smartraveller) [[VERIFY]]? What exchange rate applies to an AUD quote, and when is it fixed? Do you receive supplier commissions? Applies to any planner; no answer is given on Wedded Wonderland's commissions (deferred).

FAQ (4 to 6): What does a honeymoon planning service do? Can you plan only the honeymoon? (yes, same Wedded Advisor process) Can the honeymoon be planned alongside the destination wedding? Will the quote be in Australian dollars? Whose name should go on tickets if we travel straight after the wedding? (Smartraveller only) What should we decide before we enquire? Advisor answers in brand-facts wording only.

Close: one Advisor line in brand-facts wording (never the Wedded Advisor definition line or 'last dance'). Links /wonderland-concierge (Wedded Concierge) and /magazine as the magnet. UTMs utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=honeymoon-planning-service&utm_content=primary|secondary|magnet|closing on /wonderland-concierge and /magazine only.
avoid: Brand-facts steps 3, 4 and 5: options or availability 'actually free', the marked-up price line (awaiting sign-off), and 'someone on the ground'.
Wedded Privileges, guest room blocks, perks, upgrades, credits, VIP amenities, 'free', 'better deals', 'exclusive access'.
Transfers, availability promises, 'visited and vetted' or 'hand-picked' resorts.
Legal, marriage, name-change or passport paperwork help implied for the advisor; name and passport points only as Smartraveller states them.
Deferred business details: fee basis or amount, commissions we receive, on-the-ground support, real honeymoons, number of honeymoons or years, scale proof, named advisor, phone line.
Any price, fee amount, budget figure, saving or percentage.
Hotel, resort, airline, agency, registry or competitor names; competitor wording or images; Easy Weddings.
Competing for package terms ('honeymoon packages', 'destination honeymoon packages'); link up to /destination-honeymoon-packages instead.
Advisor claims scattered outside 'How it works' and the close; the Advisor definition line; 'last dance'; 'Wonderland Concierge' as anchor text.
'Best' or ranking language, research talk, statistics, hedge stacking.
Clichés, exclamation marks, keywords pasted into headings, em dashes, US spelling.
